conceptCapsule.title: Dynamics & Trajectory of the Centre of Mass
conceptCapsule.summary: 1. Governing Equation of Motion: $\vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = M \vec{a}_{\text{cm}} = \frac{d\vec{P}_{\text{total}}}{dt}$. Internal forces cannot accelerate or alter the velocity of the centre of mass. 2. Projectile Explosions: In mid-air explosions, internal explosive forces cancel out; the centre of mass continues along the undisturbed parabolic trajectory under gravity until external forces change. 3. Zero Horizontal External Force: When $\sum F_{\text{ext}, x} = 0$, the horizontal coordinate of the COM remains stationary ($m_1 \Delta x_1 + m_2 \Delta x_2 = 0$). This governs man-boat shifts, block-wedge sliding, and balloon-climber systems. 4. Atwood Machine COM: For two masses $m_1 > m_2$ on a fixed pulley, the individual acceleration is $a = \left(\frac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}\right)g$ and the downward acceleration of the centre of mass is $a_{\text{cm}} = \left(\frac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}\right)^2 g$.
conceptCapsule.keyFormula: $$\vec{a}_{\text{cm}} = \frac{\sum \vec{F}_{\text{ext}}}{M_{\text{total}}}, \quad \Delta x_{\text{cm}} = \frac{\sum m_i \Delta x_i}{\sum m_i} = 0, \quad a_{\text{cm, Atwood}} = \left(\frac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}\right)^2 g$$
conceptCapsule.examTrap: When applying relative velocity or displacement in man-boat or block-wedge problems, remember that the given displacement $L$ or velocity $u$ is relative to the moving object, not the ground. Always convert to the ground reference frame: $\Delta x_{\text{ground}} = L - x_{\text{recoil}}$.

questions.statement: A projectile of mass $M$ is fired from the ground with speed $u$ at an angle $	heta$ to the horizontal. At the highest point of its trajectory, it explodes into two fragments of masses $M/3$ and $2M/3$. If the lighter fragment falls vertically downward immediately after the explosion, the trajectory of the centre of mass of the system until the first fragment hits the ground is:
questions.solution:
Explosive forces are internal. The only external force acting on the system is uniform gravity $\vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = M\vec{g}$. Since $\vec{a}_{\text{cm}} = \vec{g}$, the trajectory of the centre of mass continues along the original parabolic path.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: Two blocks of masses $m_1 = 2\text{ kg}$ and $m_2 = 4\text{ kg}$ connected by a light spring are placed on a smooth horizontal floor. A constant horizontal force $F = 18\text{ N}$ acts on the $4\text{ kg}$ block. The acceleration of the centre of mass of the system is:
questions.solution:
The spring force is internal. The acceleration of the centre of mass depends solely on the external force:
$$a_{\text{cm}} = \frac{F_{\text{ext}}}{m_1 + m_2} = \frac{18}{2 + 4} = 3.0\text{ m/s}^2$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A man of mass $M = 60\text{ kg}$ stands at one end of a boat of mass $m = 120\text{ kg}$ and length $L = 6\text{ m}$ floating on calm water. The man walks from one end to the other and stops. Neglecting water resistance, the displacement of the boat relative to the water is:
questions.solution:
Since no external horizontal force acts, the centre of mass remains stationary horizontally:
$$M(L - x) - m x = 0 \implies x = \frac{M L}{M + m} = \frac{60 \times 6}{60 + 120} = 2.0\text{ m}$$
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: Two particles $A$ and $B$ initially at rest move towards each other under a mutual force of attraction. At an instant when the speed of $A$ is $v$ and the speed of $B$ is $2v$, the speed of the centre of mass of the system is:
questions.solution:
The system was initially at rest and experiences no external force (mutual attraction is purely internal). Hence $\vec{a}_{\text{cm}} = \vec{0}$ and $\vec{v}_{\text{cm}} = \vec{0}$ at all times.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A body of mass $10\text{ kg}$ is projected with an initial velocity $\vec{v}_0 = (30\hat{i} + 40\hat{j})\text{ m/s}$. At $t = 2\text{ s}$, the body explodes into two pieces of masses $4\text{ kg}$ and $6\text{ kg}$. The position vector of the centre of mass of the system at $t = 3\text{ s}$ is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
The centre of mass motion is undisturbed by internal explosion forces:
$$x_{\text{cm}}(3) = 30 \times 3 = 90\text{ m}$$
$$y_{\text{cm}}(3) = 40(3) - \frac{1}{2}(10)(3)^2 = 120 - 45 = 75\text{ m}$$
$$\vec{r}_{\text{cm}} = (90\hat{i} + 75\hat{j})\text{ m}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A block of mass $m$ is placed on the top of a smooth triangular wedge of mass $M$, height $h$, and base length $b$, which rests on a smooth horizontal floor. When the block slides down from the top to the base of the wedge, the horizontal displacement of the wedge is:
questions.solution:
Since no external horizontal force acts on the system:
$$m(b - x) - M x = 0 \implies x = \frac{m b}{M + m}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: Two particles of masses $1\text{ kg}$ and $3\text{ kg}$ are projected vertically upwards from the ground with speeds $40\text{ m/s}$ and $20\text{ m/s}$ respectively. The acceleration of their centre of mass while both are in flight is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
$$a_{\text{cm}} = \frac{m_1 g + m_2 g}{m_1 + m_2} = g = 10\text{ m/s}^2\text{ downwards}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A circular disc of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is resting on a smooth horizontal surface. A person of mass $m$ standing at the edge of the disc walks along its circumference through an angle of $2\pi$ radians. The angle through which the disc rotates during this process is:
questions.solution:
By conservation of angular momentum about the central vertical axis ($I_{\text{disc}} = \frac{1}{2}MR^2$):
$$\left(\frac{1}{2} M R^2\right)\theta = (m R^2)(2\pi - \theta) \implies \theta = \frac{2\pi m}{\frac{1}{2} M + m} = \frac{4\pi m}{M + 2m}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: Two blocks of masses $m$ and $2m$ are placed on a smooth horizontal surface and connected by an ideal spring. The system is given an initial compression $x_0$ and released from rest. At the instant the spring returns to its natural length, the ratio of the kinetic energy of mass $m$ to that of mass $2m$ is:
questions.solution:
Because initial momentum is zero and no external horizontal forces act, both blocks have equal momentum magnitudes ($p_1 = p_2 = p$).
$$\frac{K_1}{K_2} = \frac{p^2 / (2m)}{p^2 / (2(2m))} = \frac{2m}{m} = 2 : 1$$
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A uniform chain of length $L$ and mass $M$ is held vertically with its lower end just touching a table and released from rest. At an instant when length $y$ of the chain has fallen on the table, the acceleration of the centre of mass of the chain is:
questions.solution:
The length of chain still falling freely in the air is $(L - y)$ with mass $m_{\text{air}} = M\frac{L-y}{L}$. The net downward external gravitational force is $F_{\text{ext}} = m_{\text{air}} g = M g (1 - y/L)$.
$$a_{\text{cm}} = \frac{F_{\text{ext}}}{M} = g\left(1 - \frac{y}{L}\right)$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A dumbbell made of two equal masses $m$ connected by a light rigid rod of length $l$ rests on a frictionless horizontal plane. A sharp horizontal impulse $J$ is applied perpendicular to the rod at one of the masses. The speed of the centre of mass of the dumbbell immediately after the impulse is:
questions.solution:
Total mass is $M = 2m$. By the linear impulse-momentum theorem:
$$J = M v_{\text{cm}} = (2m) v_{\text{cm}} \implies v_{\text{cm}} = \frac{J}{2m}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A shell fired from a cannon explodes mid-air into several fragments of various masses. If the fragments fly off in different directions, the center of mass of all the fragments continues along:

options.text: A straight line in the direction of the heaviest fragment
The original parabolic path under gravity until external forces change
A path determined by the kinetic energy released

questions.solution:
Internal explosion forces do not alter the total linear momentum or acceleration of the centre of mass, so it proceeds along the same parabolic trajectory as the unexploded shell.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: Two identical carts $A$ and $B$, each of mass $M$, are at rest on smooth horizontal rails. A person of mass $m$ stands on cart $A$. The person jumps from cart $A$ to cart $B$ with horizontal speed $u$ relative to cart $A$. The final velocity of cart $A$ is:

options.text: $\dfrac{m u}{M + m}$ in the opposite direction
$\dfrac{M u}{M + m}$ in the opposite direction
$\dfrac{m u}{2M + m}$ in the opposite direction

questions.solution:
If cart $A$ recoils with ground speed $V_A$, the ground speed of the person is $(u - V_A)$.
Conserving horizontal momentum: $$m(u - V_A) - M V_A = 0 \implies V_A = \frac{m u}{M + m}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A system consists of three particles of masses $1\text{ kg}$, $2\text{ kg}$, and $3\text{ kg}$. Their position vectors at time $t$ are $\vec{r}_1 = t^2\hat{i}$, $\vec{r}_2 = 2t\hat{j}$, and $\vec{r}_3 = (t^2\hat{i} - t\hat{j})$ respectively. The velocity of the centre of mass of the system at $t = 1\text{ s}$ is:
questions.solution:
Velocities at $t = 1\text{ s}$: $\vec{v}_1 = 2\hat{i}$, $\vec{v}_2 = 2\hat{j}$, $\vec{v}_3 = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j}$.
$$\vec{v}_{\text{cm}} = \frac{1(2\hat{i}) + 2(2\hat{j}) + 3(2\hat{i} - \hat{j})}{6} = \frac{8\hat{i} + \hat{j}}{6} = \frac{4}{3}\hat{i} + \frac{1}{6}\hat{j}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: Two bodies of masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ are connected by a light string passing over a frictionless light pulley fixed to a ceiling (Atwood machine). If $m_1 > m_2$, the acceleration of the centre of mass of the two-body system is:
questions.solution:
Acceleration of individual blocks is $a = \left(\frac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}\right)g$.
With $m_1$ accelerating downward and $m_2$ upward: $$a_{\text{cm}} = \frac{m_1 a - m_2 a}{m_1 + m_2} = \left(\frac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}\right)a = \left(\frac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}\right)^2 g$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A person of mass $m$ is climbing up a light vertical rope hanging from a stationary hot-air balloon of mass $M$ in calm air. If the person climbs up with speed $v$ relative to the rope, the absolute upward speed of the balloon relative to the ground is:
questions.solution:
Let balloon move downward with ground speed $V$. Person moves upward with ground speed $(v - V)$.
Conserving vertical momentum: $$m(v - V) - M V = 0 \implies V = \frac{m v}{M + m} \text{ downwards}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: Two identical masses $m$ are connected by a spring of stiffness $k$. Mass 1 is pushed against a rigid vertical wall while mass 2 is pulled to compress the spring by $x_0$. When mass 2 is released, the velocity of the centre of mass of the system when mass 1 leaves the wall is:
questions.solution:
Mass 1 leaves the wall when the spring reaches natural length. By energy conservation, speed of mass 2 is $v_2 = x_0\sqrt{k/m}$ while $v_1 = 0$.
$$v_{\text{cm}} = \frac{m(0) + m v_2}{2m} = \frac{v_2}{2} = \frac{x_0}{2}\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A wooden block of mass $M$ resting on a smooth horizontal table is struck by a bullet of mass $m$ moving with speed $v$. The bullet emerges from the block with speed $v/3$. The velocity of the centre of mass of the (block + bullet) system after the collision is:
questions.solution:
Total momentum is conserved as no external force acts: $P_{\text{total}} = m v$.
$$v_{\text{cm}} = \frac{P_{\text{total}}}{M + m} = \frac{m v}{M + m}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A uniform rod of mass $M$ and length $L$ lies on a smooth horizontal table. A particle of mass $m$ moving with velocity $v_0$ perpendicular to the rod hits one end of the rod and sticks to it. The velocity of the centre of mass of the combined system after the collision is:
questions.solution:
Total initial linear momentum is $P_i = m v_0$. Since no external horizontal force acts:
$$v_{\text{cm}} = \frac{P_i}{M + m} = \frac{m v_0}{M + m}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: Two particles of masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ are moving with velocities $\vec{v}_1$ and $\vec{v}_2$. If an external force $\vec{F}_{	ext{ext}}$ acts on the system, the rate of change of total linear momentum of the system is equal to:
questions.solution:
By Newton's second law for a system of particles: $\frac{d\vec{P}}{dt} = \vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = (m_1 + m_2)\vec{a}_{\text{cm}}$. Both expressions are equivalent and correct.
Therefore, Option C is correct.
